parameters.lower_description: packed brown dirt path, warm earthy tones, NES-era retro pixel art, few colors
parameters.upper_description: rugged grey rock slabs with deep cracks and scattered stones, warm earthy tones, NES-era retro pixel art, few colors
parameters.transition_description: quarried rock face, a cut stone wall

generation.lowerFrom: meadow-01's dirt, by its base tile id, so the road is the same earth at both ends of a caravan's route; standard redraws the shared terrain close to the first, not byte for byte.

drawnAs.why: Standard rewrites the descriptions before drawing (its `enhance`, on by default) and always draws high top-down; tileset.json keeps both texts, under metadata.user_prompts and metadata.terrain_prompts.
drawnAs.upper_description: rugged grey rock slabs with wide deep cracks and sparse scattered stones in flat solid tones, no gradients or shadows
drawnAs.transition_description: quarried rock face forming a cut stone wall with large even blocks in flat uniform colour, no gradients or shadows

files.tileset.json: PixelLab's metadata for the sheet: each tile's corners (NW, NE, SW, SE as lower or upper) and its bounding_box on the sheet. Whatever draws the ground picks each tile by its four corners and cuts it out by its bounding_box, never by its wang_N name or original_position.

rejectedTags: Tilesets cannot be tagged in PixelLab; this list is how the rejects are found.

rejected.why: New earth, `packed dry earth yard`, under `bare weathered rock, cracked grey-brown stone`, transition_size 0.25: both terrains came out brown, the rock as more earth.
The same descriptions with transition_size 0: the rock a flat purple-grey field with no texture.
Meadow-01's dirt under `bare weathered rock, cracked grey-brown stone`, transition_size 0.25: grey rock, but only speckles on it.
The kept descriptions with the transition `low rock ledge with rubble over packed earth` at 0.25: light grey slabs that read as paving more than as a crag.

chosenBy: The owner, 2026-11-24, in a 400×225 camp mock-up at 3× with kept hero sets (art/mockups/highcrag-400x225-3x.png).
verified: tileset.png (/mcp/tilesets/<id>/image) and tileset.json (/mcp/tilesets/<id>/metadata) are byte-identical to a second download of each, 2026-11-24; the metadata holds 16 tiles, one for each set of four corners, each box a whole tile inside the sheet.
